arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Medellin's counsel argued the case is exceptionally important. He requested the Court hold the case. He wanted to return to Texas first.
Texas counsel argued the Court should avoid international law issues. He said the case involves state law. He emphasized the need for clarity on private rights.
Justice Rehnquist asked about creating a private right of action. He noted this is not typically covered by the Court.
Justice O'Connor suggested the Court might dismiss the case. She questioned the necessity of analyzing enforceability.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Jose Medellin asks the Court to enforce an ICJ judgment. He claims the judgment grants him individual rights. Texas officials argue the judgment does not create private rights. They say the case belongs in state courts. The dispute centers on the legal effect of international judgments.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the legal force of international judgments. It determines whether individuals can enforce ICJ rulings in U.S. courts. The outcome shapes the relationship between international law and domestic law. It affects how states handle international court decisions.
